text.p: The South Australian government on Monday approved an A$850 million key component of its proposed futuristic multi-function polis (MFP) project - the first phase of a Smart City to provide 3,700 dwellings.

Premier Dean Brown said in a statement that subject to agreement from the joint venture partners -- the Delfin Property Group Ltd /Lend Lease Ltd consortium -- construction was expected to begin early next year.

Brown said the Smart City would be a 10-year project providing up to 1,500 construction jobs and incorporating a range of 21st century living options through environmental, transport, water management, and information technology designs.
A spokesman said the government would contribute about A$25 million over 10 years towards infrastructure needs.
The announcement followed speculation the state may decide it could not afford to support the project, north of Adelaide. The federal government quit the controversial project in June.

State Infrastructure Minister John Olsen said that while the state decision provided a much-needed boost to the future of the MFP, the Smart City project now needed ratification by Delfin Lend Lease and its other major investor, the government owned national telecommunications company, Telstra.
